paper_metadata.title: Polyol-Mediated Solvation Sheath Regulation for Highly Reversible Zinc Metal Anodes
paper_metadata.abstract: Aqueous zinc batteries are hindered by hydrogen evolution and dendrites. Here, we reveal that 15 mM D-sorbitol effectively modifies the Zn2+ solvation structure, yielding 2500 hours of dendrite-free Zn plating/stripping at 2 mA cm-2.

additives.name: D-Sorbitol
additives.mechanism_summary: Displaces active water from Zn2+ inner solvation sheath and promotes (002) plane texturing.
additives.extraction_evidence: Through systematic concentration screening, we determined that 15 mM D-sorbitol exhibits optimal performance.

candidate_molecules.name: Glycerol
candidate_molecules.rationale: Tanimoto similarity of 0.43 to target. Shares structural motifs with 3 H-bond donors and 3 acceptors.
candidate_molecules.sdl_formulation_notes: Aqueous solubility limits optimal for automated liquid handling.
candidate_molecules.electrolyte_compatibility_note: Validated for sulfate chemistry; verify compatibility before using in other electrolytes; theoretically compatible with Zn(OTf)2 due to neutral non-ionic solvation sheath modulation.

ZnSO4.notes: Validated for sulfate chemistry; reconstructs Zn2+ solvation sheath by displacing active water, suppresses byproduct basic zinc sulfate (BZS) passivation, and elevates HER overpotential for uniform (002) deposition.

Zn(OTf)2.notes: Theoretically compatible with Zn(OTf)2 due to neutral non-ionic solvation sheath modulation; works synergistically with bulky OTf- anions to promote in situ ZnF2-rich SEI while displacing coordinated water.

Zn(ClO4)2.notes: Weakly coordinating ClO4- enables rapid Zn2+ desolvation kinetics; neutral polyols modulate water activity and suppress HER without impeding the ultrafast charge transfer kinetics of perchlorate.

Zn(TFSI)2.notes: In water-in-salt (WiSE) or concentrated Zn(TFSI)2 systems, polyols bind residual free water molecules, expanding the electrochemical stability window (ESW > 2.2 V) and suppressing water splitting.

ZnCl2.notes: Concentrated ZnCl2 exhibits rich chlorozinc complex anions ([ZnCl4]2-); polyols intercalate into the complex network to reduce solution viscosity, though high acidity at elevated ZnCl2 concentrations must be monitored.

Zn(CH3COO)2.notes: Acetate buffers electrolyte pH (~5-6); polyols synergistically regulate Zn2+ nucleation morphology without perturbing the mild acetate buffer equilibrium.
